claim: Stress defense and cell growth are inversely related in bulk culture analyses.
source: Stress defense and cell growth are inversely related in bulk culture analyses; however, these studies miss substantial cell-to-cell heterogeneity, thus obscuring true phenotypic relationships.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established observation from prior bulk culture studies.

claim: Bulk culture studies miss substantial cell-to-cell heterogeneity.
source: Stress defense and cell growth are inversely related in bulk culture analyses; however, these studies miss substantial cell-to-cell heterogeneity, thus obscuring true phenotypic relationships.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of bulk culture approaches in the abstract.

claim: Msn2 is a stress-activated transcription factor that regulates defense genes.
source: stress-activated Msn2 that regulates defense genes
evidence: This is stated in the abstract describing the transcription factors studied.

claim: Dot6 represses ribosome biogenesis genes during an active stress response.
source: Dot6 that represses ribosome biogenesis genes during an active stress response
evidence: This is stated in the abstract describing the function of Dot6.

claim: There is unexpected discordance between Msn2 and Dot6 behavior.
source: By tracking cells dynamically, we discovered unexpected discordance between Msn2 and Dot6 behavior that revealed subpopulations of cells with distinct growth properties.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on the dynamic tracking experiments.

claim: Discordance between Msn2 and Dot6 behavior revealed subpopulations of cells with distinct growth properties.
source: By tracking cells dynamically, we discovered unexpected discordance between Msn2 and Dot6 behavior that revealed subpopulations of cells with distinct growth properties.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on clustering analysis of transcription factor dynamics.

claim: Post-stress growth recovery was positively correlated with activation of the Dot6 repressor.
source: Surprisingly, post-stress growth recovery was positively corelated with activation of the Dot6 repressor.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract based on correlation analysis.

claim: Cells lacking Dot6 displayed slower growth acclimation after stress.
source: In contrast, cells lacking Dot6 displayed slower growth acclimation, even though they grow normally in the absence of stress.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract based on experiments with dot6∆tod6∆ mutants.

claim: Cells lacking Dot6 grow normally in the absence of stress.
source: In contrast, cells lacking Dot6 displayed slower growth acclimation, even though they grow normally in the absence of stress.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract based on growth measurements of dot6∆tod6∆ mutants.

claim: Wild-type cells with a larger Dot6 response display faster production of Msn2-regulated Ctt1 protein.
source: We show that wild-type cells with a larger Dot6 response display faster production of Msn2-regulated Ctt1 protein, separable from the contribution of Msn2.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on single-cell Ctt1 measurements.

claim: The effect of Dot6 on Ctt1 production is separable from the contribution of Msn2.
source: We show that wild-type cells with a larger Dot6 response display faster production of Msn2-regulated Ctt1 protein, separable from the contribution of Msn2.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract based on multi-factor modeling of Ctt1 production timing.

claim: Transcriptional repression during acute stress in yeast provides a protective response.
source: These results are consistent with the model that transcriptional repression during acute stress in yeast provides a protective response, likely by redirecting translational capacity to induced transcripts.
evidence: This is the proposed model stated in the abstract based on the collective findings.

claim: Transcriptional repression likely redirects translational capacity to induced transcripts.
source: These results are consistent with the model that transcriptional repression during acute stress in yeast provides a protective response, likely by redirecting translational capacity to induced transcripts.
evidence: This is the proposed mechanism stated in the abstract.

claim: Cell-to-cell variation in signaling and gene expression have been linked to differential survival of isogenic cancer cells responding to drugs.
source: For example, cell-to-cell variation in signaling and gene expression have been linked to differential survival of isogenic cancer cells responding to drugs (Lee et al., 2014; Paek et al., 2016; Shaffer et al., 2017; Inde and Dixon, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Cellular heterogeneity in bacterial growth and gene expression can produce variation in survival upon antibiotic treatment.
source: Similarly, cellular heterogeneity in bacterial growth and gene expression can produce variation in survival upon antibiotic treatment (Balaban et al., 2004; Keren et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: p53 in mammalian cells resides in the cytosol in the absence of stress but rapidly translocates to the nucleus upon activation.
source: Several canonical factors, including p53 in mammalian cells (Purvis et al., 2012; Kracikova et al., 2013; Paek et al., 2016) and Msn2 and its paralog Msn4 in fungi (Görner et al., 1998), reside in the cytosol in the absence of stress but rapidly translocate to the nucleus upon activation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Msn2 and its paralog Msn4 in fungi reside in the cytosol in the absence of stress but rapidly translocate to the nucleus upon activation.
source: Several canonical factors, including p53 in mammalian cells (Purvis et al., 2012; Kracikova et al., 2013; Paek et al., 2016) and Msn2 and its paralog Msn4 in fungi (Görner et al., 1998), reside in the cytosol in the absence of stress but rapidly translocate to the nucleus upon activation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Msn2 localization dynamics differ depending on the nature of the stress.
source: For example, Msn2 localization dynamics differ depending on the nature of the stress (Hao and O'Shea, 2012; Petrenko et al., 2013; Granados et al., 2018), and these differences impart distinct effects on different target genes (Hao and O'Shea, 2012; Hansen and O'Shea, 2013; Stewart-Ornstein et al., 2013; Hansen and O'Shea, 2015a; Hansen and O'Shea, 2015b; Hansen and O'Shea, 2016; Hansen and Zechner, 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Differences in Msn2 localization dynamics impart distinct effects on different target genes.
source: For example, Msn2 localization dynamics differ depending on the nature of the stress (Hao and O'Shea, 2012; Petrenko et al., 2013; Granados et al., 2018), and these differences impart distinct effects on different target genes (Hao and O'Shea, 2012; Hansen and O'Shea, 2013; Stewart-Ornstein et al., 2013; Hansen and O'Shea, 2015a; Hansen and O'Shea, 2015b; Hansen and O'Shea, 2016; Hansen and Zechner, 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Msn2 targets with highly responsive promoters can be induced even with brief pulses of nuclear Msn2.
source: Msn2 targets with highly responsive promoters can be induced even with brief pulses of nuclear Msn2, whereas genes with less responsive promoters require prolonged Msn2 activation (Hansen and O'Shea, 2013; Hansen and O'Shea, 2015a; Hansen and O'Shea, 2015b; Hansen and O'Shea, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Genes with less responsive promoters require prolonged Msn2 activation.
source: Msn2 targets with highly responsive promoters can be induced even with brief pulses of nuclear Msn2, whereas genes with less responsive promoters require prolonged Msn2 activation (Hansen and O'Shea, 2013; Hansen and O'Shea, 2015a; Hansen and O'Shea, 2015b; Hansen and O'Shea, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Differences in the dynamics of p53 localization can lead to distinct transcriptional outputs.
source: Similarly, differences in the dynamics of p53 localization can lead to distinct transcriptional outputs, and these distinctions correlate with differences in stress survival (Purvis et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Distinctions in p53 localization dynamics correlate with differences in stress survival.
source: Similarly, differences in the dynamics of p53 localization can lead to distinct transcriptional outputs, and these distinctions correlate with differences in stress survival (Purvis et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Substantial cell-to-cell heterogeneity in nuclear localization dynamics of stress-activated transcription factors has been observed.
source: Several studies have observed substantial cell-to-cell heterogeneity in nuclear localization dynamics of these factors (Cai et al., 2008; Cheong et al., 2011; Purvis and Lahav, 2013; Lin et al., 2015; AkhavanAghdam et al., 2016; Gasch et al., 2017; Granados et al., 2018; Li et al., 2018); however, the causes and functional effects of this variation remain poorly understood.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The causes and functional effects of cell-to-cell variation in transcription factor localization remain poorly understood.
source: Several studies have observed substantial cell-to-cell heterogeneity in nuclear localization dynamics of these factors (Cai et al., 2008; Cheong et al., 2011; Purvis and Lahav, 2013; Lin et al., 2015; AkhavanAghdam et al., 2016; Gasch et al., 2017; Granados et al., 2018; Li et al., 2018); however, the causes and functional effects of this variation remain poorly understood.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a knowledge gap.

claim: Msn2 activates defense genes that are induced in the ESR (iESR genes).
source: whereas Msn2 activates defense genes that are induced in the ESR (iESR genes), Dot6 represses growth-promoting genes involved in ribosome biogenesis that are correspondingly repressed in the ESR during stress (rESR genes) (Lippman and Broach, 2009; Bergenholm et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Dot6 represses growth-promoting genes involved in ribosome biogenesis that are correspondingly repressed in the ESR during stress (rESR genes).
source: whereas Msn2 activates defense genes that are induced in the ESR (iESR genes), Dot6 represses growth-promoting genes involved in ribosome biogenesis that are correspondingly repressed in the ESR during stress (rESR genes) (Lippman and Broach, 2009; Bergenholm et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Both Msn2 and Dot6 are controlled by the Protein Kinase A (PKA) and mTOR pathways.
source: Both factors are controlled by the Protein Kinase A (PKA) and mTOR pathways, which are generally associated with promoting growth (Figure 1A): PKA/TOR-dependent phosphorylation of Msn2 and Dot6 maintains the factors in the cytosol, whereas Msn2 and Dot6 dephosphorylation after PKA/TOR inhibition leads to their nuclear localization (Görner et al., 1998; Smith et al., 1998; Lippman and Broach, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: PKA/TOR-dependent phosphorylation of Msn2 and Dot6 maintains the factors in the cytosol.
source: Both factors are controlled by the Protein Kinase A (PKA) and mTOR pathways, which are generally associated with promoting growth (Figure 1A): PKA/TOR-dependent phosphorylation of Msn2 and Dot6 maintains the factors in the cytosol, whereas Msn2 and Dot6 dephosphorylation after PKA/TOR inhibition leads to their nuclear localization (Görner et al., 1998; Smith et al., 1998; Lippman and Broach, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Msn2 and Dot6 dephosphorylation after PKA/TOR inhibition leads to their nuclear localization.
source: Both factors are controlled by the Protein Kinase A (PKA) and mTOR pathways, which are generally associated with promoting growth (Figure 1A): PKA/TOR-dependent phosphorylation of Msn2 and Dot6 maintains the factors in the cytosol, whereas Msn2 and Dot6 dephosphorylation after PKA/TOR inhibition leads to their nuclear localization (Görner et al., 1998; Smith et al., 1998; Lippman and Broach, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Growth rate and stress tolerance are competing interests in the cell and are often antagonistically regulated.
source: Growth rate and stress tolerance are competing interests in the cell and are often antagonistically regulated: fast growing cells tend to be the most susceptible to stress and toxins, whereas slow growing or quiescent cells generally survive extreme conditions (Balaban et al., 2004; Lu et al., 2009; Zakrzewska et al., 2011; Levy et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Fast growing cells tend to be the most susceptible to stress and toxins.
source: Growth rate and stress tolerance are competing interests in the cell and are often antagonistically regulated: fast growing cells tend to be the most susceptible to stress and toxins, whereas slow growing or quiescent cells generally survive extreme conditions (Balaban et al., 2004; Lu et al., 2009; Zakrzewska et al., 2011; Levy et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Slow growing or quiescent cells generally survive extreme conditions.
source: Growth rate and stress tolerance are competing interests in the cell and are often antagonistically regulated: fast growing cells tend to be the most susceptible to stress and toxins, whereas slow growing or quiescent cells generally survive extreme conditions (Balaban et al., 2004; Lu et al., 2009; Zakrzewska et al., 2011; Levy et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The RAS-PKA pathway promotes growth and suppresses the stress response.
source: Part of this antagonistic correlation is thought to be controlled, at least under specific situations, by the RAS-PKA pathway, which promotes growth and suppresses the stress response (Smith et al., 1998; Gasch et al., 2000; Zaman et al., 2008; Zaman et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Slower growing cells in an isogenic culture displayed lower levels of the PKA allosteric activator cAMP.
source: Li et al., 2018 used single-cell microscopy to show that slower growing cells in an isogenic culture displayed lower levels of the PKA allosteric activator cAMP and that artificial activation of PKA diminished the slow growing population (Li et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Artificial activation of PKA diminished the slow growing population.
source: Li et al., 2018 used single-cell microscopy to show that slower growing cells in an isogenic culture displayed lower levels of the PKA allosteric activator cAMP and that artificial activation of PKA diminished the slow growing population (Li et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: There is a slight but statistically significant negative correlation between Msn2 nuclear localization and micro-colony growth over the subsequent 10 hr in the absence of stress.
source: They further showed a slight but statistically significant negative correlation between Msn2 nuclear localization and micro-colony growth over the subsequent 10 hr in the absence of stress.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction referring to Li et al., 2018.

claim: The microfluidics system measured cell and colony size, growth rate, and cell-cycle phase along with nuclear trans-localization of Msn2 and Dot6.
source: The system measured cell and colony size, growth rate, and cell-cycle phase along with nuclear trans-localization of two transcription factors: stress-activated Msn2 that regulates defense genes and Dot6 that represses ribosome biogenesis genes during an active stress response.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract describing the experimental system.

claim: There was substantial variation in cellular growth rates before NaCl addition.
source: As expected based on previous studies (Levy et al., 2012; Fehrmann et al., 2013; Crane et al., 2014; Li et al., 2018; Jin et al., 2019), there was substantial variation in cellular growth rates before NaCl addition, confirming that cells vary considerably in their growth properties in the absence of stress (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2A and supporting citations.

claim: Most colonies reduced their growth rate in response to NaCl stress.
source: Most colonies reduced their growth rate in response to NaCl stress (but not a mock treatment, Figure 1—figure supplement 2F), but once again there was substantial variation: some cells showed dramatic growth reduction upon NaCl, whereas others showed little to no change (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: Some cells showed dramatic growth reduction upon NaCl, whereas others showed little to no change.
source: Most colonies reduced their growth rate in response to NaCl stress (but not a mock treatment, Figure 1—figure supplement 2F), but once again there was substantial variation: some cells showed dramatic growth reduction upon NaCl, whereas others showed little to no change (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: Most cells shrunk immediately after stress despite substantial variation in size changes.
source: NaCl-induced osmotic pressure is expected to produce rapid water loss before cells acclimate, and indeed most cells shrunk immediately after stress despite substantial variation in size changes (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: Both Msn2 and Dot6 showed sporadic activation in unstressed cells, with brief and typically low levels of nuclear translocation.
source: Both factors showed sporadic activation in unstressed cells, with brief and typically low levels of nuclear translocation (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: Roughly 54% of Msn2 pre-stress peaks and 37% of Dot6 pre-stress peaks were temporally coordinated with the other factor.
source: Roughly 54% of Msn2 pre-stress peaks and 37% of Dot6 pre-stress peaks were temporally coordinated with the other factor (Figure 3B), which is significantly above chance (p<<0.0001, permutation analysis, see Methods) and suggests systemic activation of the stress response.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 3B and statistical analysis.

claim: The coordination of Msn2 and Dot6 pre-stress peaks is significantly above chance (p<<0.0001).
source: Roughly 54% of Msn2 pre-stress peaks and 37% of Dot6 pre-stress peaks were temporally coordinated with the other factor (Figure 3B), which is significantly above chance (p<<0.0001, permutation analysis, see Methods) and suggests systemic activation of the stress response.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on permutation analysis.

claim: In the vast majority of cells, NaCl provoked a dramatic and coordinated increase in nuclear localization of both Msn2 and Dot6.
source: In the vast majority of cells, NaCl provoked a dramatic and coordinated increase in nuclear localization of both Msn2 and Dot6 (acute phase).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the acute stress response.

claim: After stress Msn2 and Dot6 behavior deviated: whereas few cells showed post-stress Dot6 nuclear translocation, many cells showed asynchronous pulses of Msn2.
source: However, after stress Msn2 and Dot6 behavior deviated: whereas few cells showed post-stress Dot6 nuclear translocation, many cells showed asynchronous pulses of Msn2 (Figure 3C–F), consistent with prior work (Petrenko et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 3C-F and a supporting citation.

claim: The profiles of Dot6 nuclear pulses were often highly correlated between unstressed cells in the same colony.
source: In the course of this analysis, we realized another key difference between Msn2 and Dot6: the profiles of Dot6 nuclear pulses were often highly correlated between unstressed cells in the same colony, indicated by co-occurring peaks in two-cell colonies (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Supplementary file 1.

claim: The co-occurrence of Dot6 peaks in cells from the same colony was highly significant compared to random chance (p=9.3e-4).
source: Permutation tests showed that this was highly significant compared to random chance (p=9.3e-4, see Methods).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on permutation tests.

claim: The co-occurrence of Msn2 peaks in cells from the same colony was not significantly different from random.
source: In contrast, the co-occurrence of Msn2 peaks in cells from the same colony was not significantly different from random.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on permutation tests.

claim: Most clusters captured cells from all three biological replicates.
source: Most clusters captured cells from all three biological replicates, with the exception of cell Cluster 9 and several small clusters that were enriched for cells from one replicate (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Supplementary file 2.

claim: Six of the cell clustering patterns were clearly recapitulated in an independent experiment.
source: Six of these patterns were clearly recapitulated in an independent experiment (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cluster 11 was characterized by lower than population-median magnitude of acute-stress Dot6 nuclear translocation.
source: Cluster 11 was characterized by lower than population-median magnitude of acute-stress Dot6 nuclear translocation, whereas cells in Clusters 6 and 7 showed higher-than-median Dot6 response.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing cluster characteristics.

claim: Cells in Clusters 6 and 7 showed higher-than-median Dot6 response.
source: Cluster 11 was characterized by lower than population-median magnitude of acute-stress Dot6 nuclear translocation, whereas cells in Clusters 6 and 7 showed higher-than-median Dot6 response.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing cluster characteristics.

claim: Cluster 11 cells showed low levels of Dot6 before stress.
source: Cluster 11 cells showed low levels of Dot6 before stress, whereas cells in Clusters 9 and 6 displayed higher-than-median nuclear Msn2 and Dot6 during this phase.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing cluster characteristics.

claim: Cells in Clusters 9 and 6 displayed higher-than-median nuclear Msn2 and Dot6 before stress.
source: Cluster 11 cells showed low levels of Dot6 before stress, whereas cells in Clusters 9 and 6 displayed higher-than-median nuclear Msn2 and Dot6 during this phase.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing cluster characteristics.

claim: There was no significant correlation between cell subpopulations and cell volume changes.
source: We found no significant correlations with cell volume changes or cell-cycle phase (although there was a minor signal for cell cycle, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: There was no strong connection between cell-cycle phase and stress response.
source: This is consistent with the lack of strong connection between cell-cycle phase and stress response found in several other studies (Paek et al., 2016; Gasch et al., 2017; Bagamery et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: There was a positive correlation between pre-stress growth rate compared to post-stress growth rate.
source: Overall, there was a positive correlation between pre-stress growth rate compared to post-stress growth rate (Figure 5A); however, the association was different for subpopulations of cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5A.

claim: Cells in Cluster 11 showed slower growth rates before and after NaCl treatment.
source: Cells in Cluster 11, which were characterized by below-average Dot6 response before and during stress, showed slower growth rates before and after NaCl treatment (Figure 5B–C), and the slower growth was consistent when biological replicates were analyzed individually (p<0.02, T-test) and across multiple experiments (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5B-C and statistical analysis.

claim: Cells in Cluster 7 showed higher than average recovery growth rates.
source: In contrast, cells in Cluster 7 showed higher than average recovery growth rates – these cells were characterized by larger-than-average Dot6 nuclear localization responses and somewhat below-average nuclear translocation of Msn2 during the acute-response phase.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing cluster characteristics.

claim: Pre-stress growth rate explained only 20% of the variance in post-stress growth rate.
source: However, the most impactful single factor – pre-stress growth rate – explained only 20% of the variance in post-stress growth rate (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Supplementary file 3.

claim: Four factors contributed significantly to explain post-stress rate: pre-stress AUC of Dot6 nuclear localization, the sum of pre-stress Msn2 peak heights, the pre-stress growth rate of the cells, and the magnitude of Dot6 nuclear localization change immediately after NaCl.
source: The final regression identified four factors that contributed significantly to explain post-stress rate ('Model 3' in Supplementary file 3): pre-stress AUC of Dot6 nuclear localization, the sum of pre-stress Msn2 peak heights, the pre-stress growth rate of the cells, and the magnitude of Dot6 nuclear localization change immediately after NaCl.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Supplementary file 3.

claim: Together, four factors explained 35% of the variance in post-stress growth rate.
source: Together, these factors – all but one of which represent pre-stress cellular phenotypes – explained 35% of the variance in post-stress growth rate (Figure 6C), nearly doubling the explanatory power of any single feature alone.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6C.

claim: Cells growing faster before stress have a larger Dot6 stress-response.
source: For example, both pre-stress growth rate and Dot6 acute-stress peak height correlate with post-stress growth rate, but they also correlate with each other: cells growing faster before stress have a larger Dot6 stress-response.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing correlations.

claim: PC1 and PC3 together explained 21% of the variance in post-stress growth rate.
source: PC1 and PC3 together explained 21% of the variance in post-stress growth rate: both captured co-variation in pre-stress growth rate, acute-stress Dot6 response, and pre-stress transcription factor behaviors, indicating that these features likely reflect the same aspects of the cellular state (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6D.

claim: PC4 that is dominated by Dot6 behavior but not influenced by pre-stress growth rate explained an additional 14% of growth acclimation (p=1e-4).
source: However, PC4 that is dominated by Dot6 behavior but not influenced by pre-stress growth rate explained an additional 14% of growth acclimation (p=1e-4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6D.

claim: PC2 was dominated by pre-stress Msn2 behavior but showed no power to predict post-stress growth acclimation rates.
source: A fourth component, PC2, was dominated by pre-stress Msn2 behavior but showed no power to predict post-stress growth acclimation rates.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The dot6∆tod6∆ strain grew as wild type before stress, but showed significantly reduced growth rate after NaCl treatment.
source: Indeed, bulk-culture experiments revealed that the dot6∆tod6∆ mutant grew as wild type before stress, but showed significantly reduced growth rate after NaCl treatment (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 7A.

claim: The time to cross the Ctt1 threshold was correlated with both Msn2 and Dot6 peak heights.
source: We found that the time to cross that threshold was correlated with both Msn2 and Dot6 peak heights, which are themselves weakly correlated; however, the variance explained was significantly higher for Dot6 activity (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 7C.

claim: The variance in Ctt1 production timing explained was significantly higher for Dot6 activity than Msn2 activity.
source: We found that the time to cross that threshold was correlated with both Msn2 and Dot6 peak heights, which are themselves weakly correlated; however, the variance explained was significantly higher for Dot6 activity (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 7C.

claim: A mixed model considering both Msn2 and Dot6 factors confirmed that the contribution of Dot6 was significantly more than that of Msn2 behavior, which was only marginally significant in the model (p=0.053).
source: Indeed, a mixed model considering both factors confirmed that the contribution of Dot6 was significantly more than that of Msn2 behavior, which was only marginally significant in the model (p=0.053, Figure 7D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 7D.

claim: Dot6 is not known to regulate Ctt1 or bind its promoter.
source: Dot6 is not known to regulate Ctt1 or bind its promoter (Zhu et al., 2009), and we previously showed that dot6∆tod6∆ cells induce CTT1 transcript to higher levels than wild type during NaCl stress (Ho et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: dot6∆tod6∆ cells induce CTT1 transcript to higher levels than wild type during NaCl stress.
source: Dot6 is not known to regulate Ctt1 or bind its promoter (Zhu et al., 2009), and we previously showed that dot6∆tod6∆ cells induce CTT1 transcript to higher levels than wild type during NaCl stress (Ho et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: Aggregate analysis of all single cells in the population reported condition-specific dynamical behavior of Msn2, such as prolonged nuclear pulsing after glucose starvation versus a burst of activation before acclimating to osmotic stress.
source: Past studies focusing on aggregate analysis of all single cells in the population reported condition-specific dynamical behavior of Msn2, such as prolonged nuclear pulsing after glucose starvation versus a burst of activation before acclimating to osmotic stress (Hao and O'Shea, 2012; Petrenko et al., 2013; AkhavanAghdam et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with supporting citations.

claim: Some cells responded to the osmotic/ionic stress induced by NaCl with a large nuclear pulse of Msn2 followed by near complete acclimation, as previously reported for sorbitol-induced osmotic stress.
source: Some cells responded to the osmotic/ionic stress induced by NaCl with a large nuclear pulse of Msn2 followed by near complete acclimation, as previously reported for sorbitol-induced osmotic stress – but other cells showed extensive and prolonged Msn2 fluctuations during the acclimation phase, akin to what has been reported for glucose starvation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on the clustering analysis.

claim: Other cells showed extensive and prolonged Msn2 fluctuations during the acclimation phase, akin to what has been reported for glucose starvation.
source: Some cells responded to the osmotic/ionic stress induced by NaCl with a large nuclear pulse of Msn2 followed by near complete acclimation, as previously reported for sorbitol-induced osmotic stress – but other cells showed extensive and prolonged Msn2 fluctuations during the acclimation phase, akin to what has been reported for glucose starvation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on the clustering analysis.

claim: The different dynamics of Msn2 (and likely also Dot6) activation produce different transcriptomic outputs, even for cells responding to the same stressor in the same environment.
source: These subpopulations are obscured by aggregate analysis but have important implications, since the different dynamics of Msn2 (and likely also Dot6) activation produce different transcriptomic outputs, even for cells responding to the same stressor in the same environment.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an inference from the findings.

claim: Isogenic cells in the same culture displayed different transcriptomes upon NaCl stress, including for ESR genes, indicating that they experience the stress differently.
source: This hypothesis is consistent with past work from our lab investigating single-cell transcriptomics, in which isogenic cells in the same culture displayed different transcriptomes upon NaCl stress, including for ESR genes, indicating that they experience the stress differently (Gasch et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: The response of Dot6 explained a much larger fraction of the variance in post-stress growth rate than Msn2, when considered alone or in the multi-factor linear model.
source: Although the variety in Msn2 responses likely has important consequences on downstream gene expression, we were surprised to find little connection to growth rate, at least in the short time frames studied here. Instead, the response of Dot6 explained a much larger fraction of the variance in post-stress growth rate, when considered alone or in the multi-factor linear model (Figure 6 and Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with reference to Figure 6 and Supplementary file 3.

claim: Cells with a larger Dot6 response during the acute-stress phase showed faster production of Ctt1.
source: Cells with a larger Dot6 response during the acute-stress phase showed faster production of Ctt1, separable from Msn2 activity (Figure 7), and faster growth recovery during the acclimation phase.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with reference to Figure 7.

claim: Cells completely lacking Dot6 and its paralog show delayed Ctt1 accumulation despite having more transcript.
source: In contrast, cells completely lacking Dot6 and its paralog show delayed Ctt1 accumulation despite having more transcript (Ho et al., 2018) and dramatically reduced post-stress acclimation (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with reference to Figure 7A and a supporting citation.

claim: At least in response to NaCl treatment, transcriptional repression does not lead to reduced abundance of the encoded proteins.
source: At least in response to NaCl treatment, transcriptional repression does not lead to reduced abundance of the encoded proteins (Lee et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Transcriptional repression helps to deplete the pool of RiBi transcripts that are normally highly transcribed and translated in actively growing cells.
source: Instead, we proposed that transcriptional repression helps to deplete the pool of RiBi transcripts that are normally highly transcribed and translated in actively growing cells (Lee et al., 2011; Ho et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with supporting citations.

claim: In the absence of Dot6 repression, aberrantly abundant RiBi transcripts compete with induced mRNAs for available translational machinery, thereby delaying translation of stress-defense transcripts.
source: In the absence of Dot6 repression, aberrantly abundant RiBi transcripts compete with induced mRNAs for available translational machinery, thereby delaying translation of stress-defense transcripts.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as part of the proposed model.

claim: This yeast strain exposed to the same dose of NaCl removes a population of ribosomes from the translating pool immediately after stress.
source: In the case of NaCl, the limiting factor is unlikely to be ribosomes: we previously showed that this yeast strain exposed to the same dose of NaCl removes a population of ribosomes from the translating pool immediately after stress (Ho et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Cells preserve some ribosomes for later stress acclimation.
source: This is consistent with bacterial models of growth regulation, in which cells preserve some ribosomes for later stress acclimation (also indicating that growth rate under these conditions is not limited by ribosome availability) (Mori et al., 2017; Kim et al., 2018; Korem Kohanim et al., 2018; Remigi et al., 2019; Wu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with supporting citations.

claim: Upwards of 35% of the variance in post-stress growth rate could be explained by a multi-factorial model that includes both pre-stress and acute-stress phenotypes.
source: Using our system and the conditions studied here, upwards of 35% of the variance in post-stress growth rate could be explained by a multi-factorial model that includes both pre-stress and acute-stress phenotypes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion summarizing the modeling results.

claim: Pre-stress fluctuations in fermentative versus respirative metabolism influence how cells recover from glucose starvation, with antagonistic fitness effects depending on the situation.
source: Bagamery et al. showed that pre-stress fluctuations in fermentative versus respirative metabolism influence how cells recover from glucose starvation, with antagonistic fitness effects depending on the situation (Bagamery et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Other studies linked variation in mitochondrial function and morphology to cell age and the ability to enter quiescence, which could also influence stress responsiveness.
source: Other studies linked variation in mitochondrial function and morphology to cell age and the ability to enter quiescence, which could also influence stress responsiveness (Fehrmann et al., 2013; Laporte et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with supporting citations.

claim: Some cells in the study were fast growing before stress, showed a larger Dot6 response during stress, and acclimated faster in terms of post-stress growth rate.
source: Some cells in our study were fast growing before stress, showed a larger Dot6 response during stress, and acclimated faster in terms of post-stress growth rate; in turn, cells that were slow growing before stress had lower pre-stress Dot6 activity, lower Dot6 activation during the acute phase, and a slower growth acclimation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion summarizing the findings.

claim: Cells that were slow growing before stress had lower pre-stress Dot6 activity, lower Dot6 activation during the acute phase, and a slower growth acclimation.
source: Some cells in our study were fast growing before stress, showed a larger Dot6 response during stress, and acclimated faster in terms of post-stress growth rate; in turn, cells that were slow growing before stress had lower pre-stress Dot6 activity, lower Dot6 activation during the acute phase, and a slower growth acclimation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion summarizing the findings.

claim: Fast-growing cells may have higher biosynthetic capacity, and thus more need for ribosomes and higher transcription of RiBi genes.
source: One hypothesis is fast-growing cells may have higher biosynthetic capacity, and thus more need for ribosomes and higher transcription of RiBi genes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a hypothesis.

claim: Fast-growing cells may need to slam on the brakes of RiBi production more strongly in order to free up translational capacity.
source: These cells may therefore need to slam on the brakes of RiBi production more strongly in order to free up translational capacity.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a hypothesis.

claim: The size of the Dot6 acute-stress peak correlates with post-stress growth acclimation in a way that can be separated from pre-stress growth rate.
source: On the other hand, the size of the Dot6 acute-stress peak correlates with post-stress growth acclimation in a way that can be separated from pre-stress growth rate (Figure 6C, D and – Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with reference to Figure 6C, D and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Pre-stress growth rate did not correlate with the time to cross the Ctt1 threshold (p=0.24).
source: Interestingly, pre-stress growth rate did not correlate with the time to cross the Ctt1 threshold (p=0.24), indicating that the correlation with Dot6 is independent.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on correlation analysis.

claim: The Dot6 acute-stress peak height can be fairly well predicted by the relative pre-stress activity of Msn2 versus Dot6 (R2=0.42).
source: Interestingly, the Dot6 acute-stress peak height can be fairly well predicted by the relative pre-stress activity of Msn2 versus Dot6 (R2=0.42, Figure 7—figure supplement 1), again linking acute-stress behavior to pre-stress cell states.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: 221 cells passing quality control metrics were analyzed.
source: In total, we analyzed 221 cells passing these filters, collected from the three independent biological replicates.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the dataset.

claim: Images of each field of view were captured at 6-min intervals.
source: Images of each field of view were captured at 6-min intervals.
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing the imaging protocol.

claim: The analysis was limited to colonies consisting of no more than two cells at the time points leading up to NaCl exposure.
source: First, to ensure that colony growth rates were representative of nuclear localization dynamics within individual cells, we limited our analysis to colonies consisting of no more than two cells at the time points leading up to NaCl exposure.
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing quality control filters.

claim: Most of these two-cell colonies represented mother/daughter cells and therefore had clear shared life histories.
source: Most of these two-cell colonies represented mother/daughter cells and therefore had clear shared life histories.
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing the two-cell colonies.

claim: Thirty cells were excluded from post-stress measures due to cell adhesion issues that skewed colony size measures.
source: Thirty cells were excluded from post-stress measures due to these cell adhesion issues that skewed colony size measures.
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing quality control.

claim: Six cells (2.7% of total cells) had no apparent post-stress growth and were excluded from post-stress growth rate measures.
source: Another six cells (2.7% of total cells) had no apparent post-stress growth and the calculated slope was therefore dominated by noise in pixel number. This resulted in either a negative or near zero slope and consequently did not provide an informative growth rate measure when taking the natural log of the change in colony size. Consequently, these six cells were also excluded from post-stress growth rate measures.
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing quality control.

claim: Experiments with AGY1813 (n=3) resulted in an analysis of 228 cells.
source: Experiments with AGY1813 (n=3) had the same quality control filters applied to them, with an additional metric applied to exclude cells expressing persistent, high iRFP signal throughout the time course (11 cells). This resulted in an analysis of 228 cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing the AGY1813 experiments.

claim: Nuclear localization of Msn2 and Dot6 was measured by taking the pixel intensity of the top 5% of pixels in the cell divided by the median pixel intensity within the circle mask identified for each cell.
source: Nuclear localization of Msn2 and Dot6 was measured by taking the pixel intensity of the top 5% of pixels in the cell divided by the median pixel intensity within the circle mask identified for each cell, similar to other studies (Cai et al., 2008; Hao and O'Shea, 2012; Petrenko et al., 2013; Lin et al., 2015; AkhavanAghdam et al., 2016; Gasch et al., 2017; Granados et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section with supporting citations.

claim: Two standard deviations from the mean of the distribution was used as a threshold for calling nuclear localization peaks.
source: Specifically, two standard deviations from the mean of the distribution of was used as a threshold.
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing peak calling.

claim: There were 18 cells where Msn2 signal was focused but outside the nucleus (likely in the vacuole), and these cells were excluded from subsequent regression modeling.
source: There were 18 cells were this was observed visually. Since the impact of this signal was uncertain, these cells were excluded from subsequent regression modeling (i.e. Figures 5A—7).
evidence: This is stated in the Methods section describing quality control for regression modeling.
